subject: Human Body
title: The Gut-Brain Connection
description: A 60-second lesson on The Gut-Brain Connection.

hook.text: Butterflies in your stomach before a speech? That's your gut and brain talking to each other in real time.

buildup.text: The vagus nerve connects the gut to the brain directly. It carries signals in both directions constantly.

discovery.text: 90% of serotonin, the mood chemical, is produced in the gut. Your intestines make more of it than your brain does.

twist.text: Gut bacteria influence serotonin production. Disrupting the microbiome can alter mood and anxiety levels.

climax.text: The gut is sometimes called the 'second brain.' It has its own nervous system with over 500 million neurons.

punchline.text: Your gut feelings are literally that: feelings from your gut.

quiz.question: Where is most of the body's serotonin produced?
